entries.title: I Corinthians 8:1
segments: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but love edifieth.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:2
segments: If any man thinketh that he knoweth anything, he knoweth not yet as he ought to know;

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:3
segments: but if any man loveth God, the same is known by him.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:4
segments: Concerning therefore the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is [anything] in the world, and that there is no God but one.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:5
segments: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth; as there are gods many, and lords many;

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:6
segments: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we unto him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:7
segments: Howbeit there is not in all men that knowledge: but some, being used until now to the idol, eat as [of] a thing sacrificed to an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:8
segments: But food will not commend us to God: neither, if we eat not, are we the worse; nor, if we eat, are we the better.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:9
segments: But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to the weak.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:10
segments: For if a man see thee who hast knowledge sitting at meat in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:11
segments: For through thy knowledge he that is weak perisheth, the brother for whose sake Christ died.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:12
segments: And thus, sinning against the brethren, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, ye sin against Christ.

entries.title: I Corinthians 8:13
segments: Wherefore, if meat causeth my brother to stumble, I will eat no flesh for evermore, that I cause not my brother to stumble.
